# Bellwether Creamery

> Slow-churned ice cream in small batches, with fruit and dairy from growers we know by name. Two gallons at a time, churned every morning at the Old Mill kitchen.

Bellwether Creamery is a small-batch ice cream company with three scoop shops. We churn two gallons at a time using fruit and dairy from local growers. Sixteen flavors in rotation, including dairy-free and sorbet options. Pints, bars, sandwiches, party packs, and merch available for overnight shipping.

## Pages

- [Home](https://bellwethercreamery.com/) — Featured flavors, seasonal highlights, shop gallery, gift cards
- [Flavors](https://bellwethercreamery.com/flavors.html) — Full range: pints, seasonal, dairy-free, sorbets, bars, sandwiches, party packs, van loot
- [Locations](https://bellwethercreamery.com/locations.html) — Three scoop shops (Old Mill, Riverside, Harbor Green), hours, local delivery within 8 miles
- [Our Story](https://bellwethercreamery.com/story.html) — How we started, our churning process, ingredient sourcing

## Key Facts

- Founded: Year one started with one machine in a rented kitchen
- Batch size: 2 gallons
- Flavors in rotation: 16 (including dairy-free and sorbets)
- Scoop shops: 3 (Old Mill, Riverside, Harbor Green)
- Churning: Daily, on site at the Old Mill kitchen
- Dairy-free: Churned on a separate line with its own equipment
- Shipping: Overnight with dry ice, free over $60
- Local delivery: Same-day within 8 miles of Old Mill

## Shop Locations

- **Old Mill** — 41 Mill Race Lane. Open daily, 11am–10pm. The original kitchen where everything is made.
- **Riverside** — 208 Towpath Street. Open daily, 12pm–11pm. Patio seating along the water.
- **Harbor Green** — 7 Quayside Row. Open daily, 12pm–9pm. Small counter, no seating.

## Process

1. Steep first — vanilla pods, mint leaves, and coffee go into the cream overnight
2. Churn slow, churn cold — slower churning works less air into the base for denser texture
3. Fold in by hand — ripples and mix-ins go in with a paddle, not a machine

## Sourcing

Dairy arrives twice a week from two nearby farms. Fruit is seasonal and local. Cocoa, vanilla, and pistachios are sourced from importers who trace lot origins.
